content.text: {"summary":"The web crew will set up a tiny Node project with the split math and its test, then build the page that shows what each person pays as you type.","items":[{"text":"Set up the Node project, split math module and its test","assignee":"a-semic","teamId":"f1c-web-crew","brief":"Set up a plain Node project with no dependencies. Add a tiny server using only Node's built-in http module that serves a static page. Put the split math in its own module: given bill amount, tip % and number of people, return the tip, the total and what each person pays, and handle bad input like zero people or empty fields safely. Add a node:test test for the math (normal cases, rounding to cents, bad input). Write `run: node server.js` (or the real start command) as one line in `.project`. In CLAUDE.md's \"Project-specific rules\", write the stack, how to run it and how to test it (e.g. `node --test`). Done when the server starts, serves a placeholder page, and the tests pass.","parallel":false,"report":false},{"text":"Build the tip splitter page that updates as you type","assignee":"a-semic","teamId":"f1c-web-crew","brief":"Build the page served by the Node server: three inputs for bill amount, tip % and number of people, and a result showing the tip, the total and what each person pays. The result updates live as the user types, using the same split math module (shared with the browser, no copy of the math). Show a friendly message instead of a broken number when input is missing or invalid. Keep it simple and clean. Done when the page works in a browser from the run command and the existing tests still pass.","parallel":false,"report":false}],"feature":{"name":"Tip splitter","description":"A page where you enter the bill, tip % and number of people and instantly see what each person pays.","ships":true}}
